lookback_notes: NOT_FOUND. The audit area for Missing Patient Record (p. 3) states no observation/look-back window; it addresses availability of the patient record for review rather than a period of observation ending on an assessment reference date. The document as a whole applies to service dates 01/01/2013 through 10/31/2025, but that is a service-date scope, not an assessor look-back window.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the patient record is not available for review, claims for all dates of service associated with the patient record will be disallowed.

federal_coding_rules.rule: In applying this criterion during an audit, OMIG will review and consider any relevant contemporaneous documentation maintained and available in the provider's records to substantiate a claim.

source.quote: OMIG will review and consider any relevant contemporaneous documentation maintained and available in the provider’s records to substantiate a claim.

federal.criterion: The patient record must be available for review at audit; its unavailability results in disallowance of claims for all dates of service associated with that record.

source.quote: If the patient record is not available for review, claims for all dates of service associated with the patient record will be disallowed.

federal.notes: Stated as the OMIG Audit Criteria for Area 1 (Missing Patient Record).

state_deltas.delta: This is a New York State (OMIG) audit protocol for the Assisted Living Program; Area 1 requires the patient record to be available for review, citing 10 NYCRR § 766.6, 18 NYCRR §§ 485.11(a), 487.10(c), 488.10(c)(1), and the NYS Medicaid Program ALP Manual, Policy Guidelines Version 2006-1, Section II.
